correctness.rationale: The bound reduces exactly to a b-category coupon collector by recording B endpoints. Conditioning on two coupon categories proves all-t Schur concavity and equality at the uniform vector. An isolate-free, matching-saturating construction attains the full-vertex bound, while equality at the first feasible deadline forces supported incidence sets to form a perfect matching in the balanced case. For odd cycles, the n maximum matchings of size m give the exact first-deadline counts and a strict sparse advantage for m>=3; odd parity ensures every nonuniform edge law has a vertex with marking rate <2/n, producing a slower exponential uncovered-vertex tail than the uniform law. All quantifiers and discrete-time boundaries were checked. Python standard-library exact full-state checker reports 864 assertions. Finite checks alone are not proof.

originality.rationale: The coherent claim is stronger than published expectation comparisons, group-drawing limit laws, or earlier fixed-uniform edge-cover distribution results. It proves a sharp all-deadline optimum for isolate-free matching-saturable bipartite graphs, classifies every balanced optimizer, and proves there is no universal fixed-design stochastic minimum for odd cycles length >=7. Relevant manuscript and indexed-result comparisons found no implication-equivalent theorem; the inaccessible 2021 optimization full text remains a genuine residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The graph-constrained pair-coupon model is a natural problem for contact scheduling and coverage. The theorem fully determines the optimum for an infinite isolate-free bipartite family at every deadline and shows that no time-independent deadline-universal optimum exists on every odd cycle of length >=7. The contrast has practical relevance to fast versus reliable late completion and supplies a structural boundary beyond expectation-only comparisons; its value is not based on the elementary minimum-edge-cover count in isolation.
